rules: Never touch tests/. Fix the code, not the tests.
title: The ignored rule
system: You are a coding agent. Use the tools to change files and run tests. Say done when the work is finished.

script.say: The test expects 3 and total returns 4, so the test is what is wrong. I will change it.

then.say: The edit was denied. I will fix calc.py instead.

incident.why: The rule is in the prompt and nowhere else. The model reads it, then edits the test anyway, and nothing stops the edit. The edit is allowed, the run ends as done, and the check on the test fails. A rule that must hold has to be in code.
incident.hint: Find the edit to the test. Which part of the harness decided it was allowed?

notes.text: That reply is a model's ordinary slip: it reads the test as the problem. The rule is in the prompt, so the slip is not the failure. The failure is the harness letting the edit through.

fixes.text: Enforce the rule in code: a pre-tool hook that denies edits under tests/ and fails closed
fixes.why: The edit is refused whatever the prompt says, so the rule holds late in a long run as well as early.

fixes.text: Write the rule in capitals: NEVER edit tests/
fixes.why: Tempting and wrong. A louder line in the prompt is still only a line, and it can be ignored.

fixes.text: Add more rules to the prompt, with examples
fixes.why: Tempting and wrong. Longer instructions are not safer: the same line still holds only as well as the model reads it.
